facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1956 per two sources; the Shoshone County list marks it gone. No source describes what, if anything, remains.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Dominion name is shared. The Shoshone County list places a Dominion Mountain / Dominion Peak site on the state line in township 46N-7E-4, and the FFLOS list gives it coordinates 47.36733 -115.57757, far north of this site's 47.17809 -115.51969. Not the same site, so the Dominion Mountain footing described in a January 2026 Bonner County Daily Bee article is not used for this lookout. The Bluff sits in 44N-7E-12.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. Three sources agree on the 1935 L-4 cab, the 1956 loss and the patrol tower two miles south atop Dominion Point. Identity risk: a Bonner County Daily Bee article of 31 January 2026 (https://bonnercountydailybee.com/news/2026/jan/31/group-seek-to-identify-honor-fire-lookout-crews/) describes a concrete footing at a former 'Dominion Mountain Lookout' and a 1933 lookout named Charles Nelson. That is the Dominion Mountain / Dominion Peak site on the state line (46N-7E-4, FFLOS 47.36733 -115.57757), not this Bluff site (44N-7E-12, 47.17809 -115.51969), so it is excluded. No staffing is documented for the Bluff anywhere read. Brief record checked (county Shoshone, ground, destroyed 1956): no correction. Not read: the Dominion Point patrol entry (listed on the Shoshone County page without detail), Forest Service records, any photograph. Today: no source describes the site, and the 2026 article concerns a different site.
